claim: Measured head-to-head in guideline versus rules against the official Cold Clear 2, a Cold Clear 2 fork, Hoiko and clys.
hero: Same pieces, both seats, guideline versus rules over the Tetris Bot Protocol. Cold Clear 2 had a {{cc2Ms}} ms window per move at {{cc2Pps}} PPS paired turns; Attax played its field-40 profile with exact bag speculation. Cold Clear 2 generated more attack per piece ({{cc2RivalApp}} to {{cc2App}}); Attax won on survival. Win rate {{cc2WinRate}} (95% interval {{cc2Low}}–{{cc2High}}) on seeds {{cc2Seeds}} — fresh seeds, never used for tuning.
profiles: Cold Clear 2. The official upstream engine by MinusKelvin (commit {{cc2Upstream}}) played over the Tetris Bot Protocol under guideline rules, with a {{cc2Ms}} ms window per move and {{cc2Pps}} PPS paired turns; the engine process is suspended while Attax searches, so both sides get the same wall-clock window. Attax played its field-40 profile with exact bag speculation. Seeds {{cc2Seeds}} were played from both seats; Attax won {{cc2Seats}} by seat, with no draws. Cold Clear 2 generated more attack per piece ({{cc2RivalApp}} to {{cc2App}}); Attax won on survival, clearing {{cc2Lines}} lines to Cold Clear 2's {{cc2RivalLines}}. All recorded games were replay-verified.

Cold Clear 2 fork. chouhy's fork of Cold Clear 2, measured the same way on seeds {{forkSeeds}}, played from both seats; Attax won {{forkSeats}} by seat, with no draws. Attax generated more attack per piece ({{forkApp}} to {{forkRivalApp}}). The fork cleared more lines ({{forkRivalLines}} to {{forkLines}}); Attax won more games. All recorded games were replay-verified.

Hoiko. Hoiko used preset we, beam {{hoikoBeam}}, depth {{hoikoDepth}} and a {{hoikoPreview}}-piece preview, with adaptation off. Both sides got the same pieces and locked one piece per {{hoikoPace}} ms. Seeds {{hoikoSeeds}} were never used for tuning. Swapped seats replayed the same game, so each seed counts once.

clys. citrus610's Monte Carlo beam search bot ran its default configuration (width {{clysWidth}}, depth {{clysDepth}}, branch {{clysBranch}}, {{clysThreads}} thread). Seeds {{clysSeeds}} were played from both seats; Attax won {{clysSeats}} by seat, with no draws. clys generated more attack per piece; Attax won on survival, clearing {{clysLines}} lines to clys's {{rivalLines}}. The external-bot referee uses the guideline attack table without combo or perfect-clear attack, {{previews}} previews, hold and {{clysPps}} PPS paired turns. clys gets a {{clysMs}} ms search window; Attax completes fixed work without a deadline. Lanes use dedicated CPU cores, with one bot thinking at a time per lane. Neither bot sees pending garbage over TBP. All recorded games were replay-verified.
unmeasured: Direct games against the real Hoiko.exe. The benchmark machine has no Wine. The replica matched the .exe on {{parityMain}} moves (seed {{paritySeed}}) and {{parityOther}} each (seeds {{paritySeeds}}).
Hoiko with its wall-clock adaptation on.

Cold Clear 2 and its fork outside the {{cc2Ms}} ms window, {{cc2Pps}} PPS pace and this rules profile. The game-level Wilson interval is descriptive: independent units are the seed pairs. Realtime inputs and network latency were not measured.

clys outside its default configuration, {{clysMs}} ms window and this rules profile. Its evaluator values combo/perfect clears that the referee does not score. This is not an equal-compute ranking. Attax sees only {{attaxRows}} rows and ignores bag state; clys sees {{clysRows}} rows and can use bag state. The game-level Wilson interval is descriptive: independent units are {{clysSeedCount}} seed pairs. Stochastic search and time slicing can change fresh scores. No game reached the {{turnCap}}-turn cap. Realtime inputs and network latency were not measured.
